The flight of the Portuguese royal family and court from Lisbon to Brazil, as Napoleon's army invaded Portugal. The fleet sailed on 29 November 1807 under British naval escort, days before the French reached Lisbon. It carried the mad Queen Maria I, the prince regent João, and thousands of nobles and officials.

The court landed at Salvador in January 1808 and settled in Rio de Janeiro in March. It was the only time a European monarchy ruled from one of its colonies.

It changed Brazil fast:

  • Brazil's ports were opened to friendly nations, mainly Britain.
  • A national bank, a printing press, a royal library, military and medical schools and a botanical garden were set up.
  • In 1815 Brazil was raised to a kingdom equal with Portugal.

João went home in 1821 under pressure from Portugal. His son Pedro stayed behind and in 1822 declared Brazil independent, with himself as emperor. Brazil thus left Portugal far more peacefully than Spanish America left Spain.
